text:
maria: :rotating_light: heads up - enterprise customer (acct_acme) reporting p99 spike from 110ms -> 720ms after last runtime deploy in us-west. They see it on chat/completions route. link: https://console.redwood/acme/alerts
kevin: which model/version and sequence lengths? any recent flags changed in the build?
maria: model: gpt-small-open-2026-09 @v1.7. compile flag PR merged yesterday toggled `-DUSE_SDPA=1` for nv_kernel heuristics. typical seqs 512-1024 for them.
dmitri: ok that matches a hypothesis: SDPA kernel performs worse for mid/long sequences on current nvcc codegen in prod. can you paste a latency trace and kernel selection log?
maria: paste logs below (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-17T12:02:14Z] req_id=abc123 model=gpt-small-open-2026-09 seq=768 selected_kernel=sdpa_v2 compile_flags=USE_SDPA=1
[2026-03-17T12:02:14Z] token_latencies_ms=[2,3,4,...,120,180,210] p95=550 p99=720
[2026-03-17T12:02:16Z] req_id=abc124 model=gpt-small-open-2026-09 seq=64 selected_kernel=flashattn_v1 p95=35 p99=60
```
kevin: that is telling — sdpa_v2 being chosen for seq=768 and showing high per-token latencies. did kernel selector use sequence histogram?
lee: selector currently picks by model_arch + compiled_flags + avg_seq_bucket. looks like avg_seq_bucket skewed because of sampling window. SDPA wins compile-score but bad for tail.
support-sarah: customer is requesting an immediate mitigation, they are on a paid SLA.
maria: I initiated a routing override for acct_acme to route to model variant pinned to v1.6 (pre-SDPA compile) via admin API: `POST /admin/routes/override` {"customer":"acct_acme","model":"gpt-small-open-2026-09","variant":"v1.6"} — that reduced p99 back to ~60ms.
deploy-bot: rollback started for routing override id=ro-9981 by maria at 2026-03-17T12:10:45Z
dmitri: good short-term. longer term we need kernel selector fix or revert compile flag. can we temporarily flip the runtime feature flag to disable SDPA globally while we patch heuristics?
lee: I can push a feature flag toggle to the runtime cluster: `REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFER=flashattn` per-region. plan: set for us-west-prod only. doing it now.
maria: command run:
```
kubectl -n runtime exec config-svc -- curl -XPOST http://localhost:8080/flags -d '{"REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFER":"flashattn","scope":"us-west-prod"}'
```
lee: flag applied. monitoring.
kevin: metrics?
maria: after toggle p95 ~40ms p99 ~65ms for acct_acme. customer confirmed degraded experience fixed. :thumbsup:
dmitri: parallel task: update kernel selector to consider seq_len_histogram tail weights and cost_model delta per-batch. i'll open a PR to change heuristic and add unit tests and perf benchmark. assigning to @dmitri. ETA 48h for patch + canary.
dmitri: PR: https://git.redwood/infer/runtime/pulls/4325 - adds tail-aware scoring, falls back to flashattn if predicted tail cost > 1.4x
kevin: also create a quick hotfix to revert compile flag in the build pipeline (safe revert) as a rollback if selector patch regresses. owner: @kevin.
lee: ops note — add a canary route that samples 1% traffic with new selector, check p95/p99 and kernel selection histogram before global rollout. I'll set up dashboards.
support-sarah: I'll update customer and confirm SLA timeline. they asked for RCA to include why sampling window missed tail.
maria: quick repro steps for QA/eng:
1) spawn a long-seq workload: `python benchmarks/stream_tokens.py --seq 768 --qps 10 --model gpt-small-open-2026-09 --variant v1.7`
2) tail kernel logs: `kubectl logs -l app=infer --since=5m | grep selected_kernel | grep sdpa`
3) measure p95/p99 via /metrics or grafana dashboard (dashboard: runtime.attention.kernel_latency)

expected: with SDPA enabled, p99 should spike for seq >=512 on current build.

mitigation checklist we agreed:
- [x] emergency routing override to v1.6 (maria)
- [x] region feature flag prefer=flashattn (lee)
- [ ] selector patch PR + bench (dmitri)
- [ ] safe-build revert plan (kevin)
- [ ] canary + dashboards (lee)

kevin: any risk toggling flashattn globally? memory/regression concerns?
dmitri: flashattn uses more scratch memory but we've tested capacity; us-west has headroom. still we should monitor OOMs during canary.
lee: added alert: runtime.attention.kernel_ooms > 0 for 5m -> pager to eng-runtime oncall.
maria: customer update: "Thanks, latency restored, we're monitoring. Please keep us posted on root cause and long-term fix."
support-sarah: closing the escalation ticket is blocked until selector PR merges and we have postmortem. I'll draft the RCA and include kernel logs and timeline.
maria: thanks all — tagging @oncall for visibility :eyes:
kevin: nice work triage team. let's sync in mob sync tomorrow 10am to review selector heuristics and testing strategy.
lee: I'll paste the quick heuristic change diff in the PR and include perf data.
dmitri: note for postmortem: add test harness that runs seq distribution workloads across kernels nightly to catch regressions earlier.
maria: marking thread resolved for support but leaving open until postmortem is published.
